From scenario to evidence

Connect the right data

Each input has a clear replacement path. Start with a route and a set of assumptions, then bring in dated supplier prices, flight performance and confirmed supply limits as they become available.

What to collect and where to get it

Model inputAvailable nowReplacement data
Airport geographyCoordinates for 67 airports, sourced from OurAirports. The map uses Natural Earth boundaries.OurAirports provides a public starting point. Confirm the airport and operational routing against the flight plan.
Delivered jet-fuel priceA common jet-fuel base plus regional, distance, service and tax adjustments.Request dated into-plane offers from airport fuel suppliers, airlines or fuel brokers. Record airport, currency, unit, fees, tax treatment, validity and supplier. Import comparable prices in USD/t.
Flight performanceTwo generic aircraft profiles derive fuel use from distance and time.Use operator flight-planning outputs for the chosen aircraft, payload, weather and routing. OpenAP can support an initial research calibration.
Fuel reserve and weight limitsExplicit reserve, tank, takeoff and landing assumptions.Use the operator's approved reserve policy, aircraft limits, payload plan and airport-specific performance restrictions.
Available upliftAn adjustable supply cap for each visit, with individual leg overrides.Confirm allocated tonnes and the uplift window with each supplier. Add delivery-rate, slot or storage constraints when the operation requires them.
Jet-fuel market contextThe common scenario base is transparent and editable.EIA's US Gulf Coast jet-fuel series gives public wholesale context with its own reporting lag. Regional assessments from Platts or Argus require the relevant access. Airport prices still need local delivery terms.

The decision

Where should this rotation buy fuel?

You choose the airports and their order. The model chooses how much fuel to buy at each stop while meeting fuel balance, reserve, tank, weight and supply constraints. It compares that plan with buying the minimum needed on each leg, using the same final fuel target.

A single leg checks feasibility and cost. Several legs reveal whether a lower price at an earlier stop justifies carrying extra fuel.

Reproducible inputs

Keep the assumptions with the result

The dataset download includes all 67 airport records, price components, aircraft profiles, formulas and replacement sources. The model export records the route, inputs and calculated fuel plan so the result can be rerun.
